Only the initial presentation area and five of eight affirmative base attempts were reached. Negative, W-question, OR-question, mixed-practice, picture-book, comprehension, transfer, and recap are absent, so strict phase completion and picture-book application fail and no FINISH is possible.

Teacher-language closure is not the cause of failure: admitted teacher turns carry receipts with no unlicensed forms, and the rejected turn adds no admitted learner-facing language. The defect is exact event realization and phase binding.

The learner behavior remains plausible for the stated developmental level: four early cross-instance selections followed by one visually similar fork/knife confusion is neither arbitrary sabotage nor an alarm pathology. Recovery is wholly unknown because remediation was rejected.

No closure change is supportable. Early correct selections cannot establish acquisition because the run is incomplete and, more fundamentally, the canonical log does not establish exact delivery of the eight frozen model turns.
